results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if database identifier is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Discover the right database using NOTION_SEARCH_NOTION_PAGE (use a narrow query and paginate with has_more/next_cursor).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Confirm schema, writable properties, and select/status options using NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE (ensure the identifier is a database, not a page).

[Required] [Prerequisite]: Find candidate existing rows and build a stable match-key→row map using NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER (paginate via start_cursor/has_more; define a consistent policy for multiple matches).
[Optional (if you must verify before overwriting or inspect ambiguous matches)] [Prerequisite]: Load current properties for the chosen row using NOTION_FETCH_ROW (use page_id).
[Required] [Step]: Create-or-update each item idempotently using NOTION_UPSERT_ROW_DATABASE (store returned row/page identifiers for reruns; only send schema-valid typed properties).
[Optional (if only patching a few fields or upsert validation is sensitive)] [Step]: Apply targeted edits using NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE (update only the necessary properties).

[Fallback (if filtered matching is not feasible due to schema/filter errors)] [Step]: Scan rows using NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE (page_size up to 100; paginate) then continue with NOTION_UPSERT_ROW_DATABASE and/or NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE.

[Optional (if updating page metadata or appending rich body content)] [Next Step]: Apply page changes using NOTION_UPDATE_PAGE and/or append blocks using NOTION_ADD_MULTIPLE_PAGE_CONTENT (chunk to tool limits).
[Required] [Next Step]: Re-run NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER (or NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE) to confirm persisted values and detect unintended duplicates.
known_pitfalls: [NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE] Max 100 rows per call; relation-like properties may appear partial even when more data exists, so don’t treat visible related items as complete without additional checks.
[NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE] 400 validation_error if a page identifier (or malformed identifier) is passed as database_id; 404 object_not_found if the database is wrong or not shared.
[NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER] 400 validation_error for missing/case-mismatched properties; title values can be split across arrays and large results may be offloaded, so parse defensively.
[NOTION_UPSERT_ROW_DATABASE] Validation can fail when an update payload is omitted or types don’t match schema; switch to NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE for minimal patches.
[NOTION_ADD_MULTIPLE_PAGE_CONTENT] Limit of 100 blocks per call; [NOTION_UPDATE_PAGE] properties must be typed objects (not raw strings) and only for properties present on the page.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Paginate NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE until has_more is false.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
all_rows=[]
start_cursor=None
while True:
  args={"database_id":database_id,"page_size":100}
  if start_cursor: args["start_cursor"]=start_cursor
  res,err=run_composio_tool("NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE",args)
  if err: raise RuntimeError(err)
  data=(res or {}).get("data",{})
  all_rows.extend(data.get("results",[]))
  if not data.get("has_more"): break
  start_cursor=data.get("next_cursor")
```

NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE.description: Fetches a Notion database's structural metadata (properties, title, etc.) via its `database_id`, not the data entries; `database_id` must reference an existing database.

database_id.description: Required. The unique identifier of the Notion database in UUID format (e.g., '2ec43c10-7ecd-8159-a8f4-ff16630df66c') or unhyphenated 32-char hex (e.g., '2ec43c107ecd8159a8f4ff16630df66c'). Must be a DATABASE ID, not a page ID. Linked databases are NOT supported - use the original source database ID. To find database IDs: use NOTION_SEARCH_NOTION_PAGE with filter_value='database', or extract from database URLs (notion.so/{database_id}).

NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE_WITH_FILTER.description: Tool to query a Notion database with server-side filtering, sorting, and pagination. Use when you need to retrieve a subset of rows by property, date, status, or other conditions.

anyOf.description: Sort by a system timestamp field (created or last edited time).

sorts.description: List of sort criteria in order of precedence. Use PropertySort for database properties (with property field) and TimestampSort for system timestamps (with timestamp='created_time' or 'last_edited_time'). IMPORTANT: To sort by page creation or last edited time, you MUST use the TimestampSort format with timestamp='created_time' or timestamp='last_edited_time', NOT property names like 'Created' or 'Last Edited'. Common timestamp field name variations (Created, creation time, Last Edited, etc.) will be automatically converted to the correct format.

filter.description: PREREQUISITE: Call NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE first to discover property names and types. Filter type keys MUST match the property's actual type in the schema. Each filter object MUST contain exactly ONE filter type key. For multiple conditions, use compound filters: {"and": [{"property": "Name", "title": {...}}, {"property": "Description", "rich_text": {...}}]}. 'title' IS A RESERVED PROPERTY NAME: 'title' always refers to the database's built-in primary title column (type 'title', NOT 'select' or 'rich_text'). Even custom properties named 'title' are treated as the built-in title column. FILTER TYPE MUST MATCH SCHEMA TYPE: Property names are NOT reliable indicators of type. A property named 'Status' could be type 'select' in one database but type 'status' in another. 'select' is for dropdowns; 'status' is ONLY for Notion's built-in Status property with workflow groups. SELECT/STATUS/MULTI_SELECT VALUES ARE CASE-SENSITIVE: Option names must match EXACTLY as defined in the database schema, including capitalization and emoji prefixes (e.g., 'Done' not 'done', '✅ Done' not 'Done'). Common mistake: using 'done' when the actual option is 'Done'. Check the database schema for exact option names. Valid filter type keys: title, rich_text, number, checkbox, select, multi_select, status, date, people, files, url, email, phone_number, relation, created_by, created_time, last_edited_by, last_edited_time, formula, unique_id, rollup, verification, timestamp. FORMULA FILTERS: Structure: {'property': '<name>', 'formula': {<result_type>: {<condition>: <value>}}}. Result types: 'string' (rich_text conditions), 'number' (numeric conditions), 'date' (date conditions), 'checkbox' (boolean conditions). The result type MUST match the formula's actual output type. If the formula property value shows type 'boolean', use 'checkbox' in the filter (API naming mismatch). Some complex formulas are unfilterable ('Unable to filter based on a formula of unknown type') - use client-side filtering instead. NOTE: 'text' is NOT valid - use 'rich_text' for text properties or 'title' for title properties. SYSTEM TIMESTAMP FILTERS: Use simplified format: {"created_time": {"on_or_after": "2024-01-01"}} - auto-transformed to correct API format. Filter structure for database properties: {"property": "<property_name>", "<filter_type>": {"<condition>": "<value>"}}. Common conditions by type: title/rich_text: equals, contains, starts_with, ends_with, is_empty, is_not_empty; select/status: equals, does_not_equal, is_empty, is_not_empty; number: equals, does_not_equal, greater_than, less_than, greater_than_or_equal_to, less_than_or_equal_to, is_empty, is_not_empty; checkbox: equals (true/false); date: equals, before, after, on_or_before, on_or_after, is_empty, is_not_empty, past_week, past_month, past_year, next_week, next_month, next_year; relation: contains, does_not_contain (both require a valid page UUID), is_empty, is_not_empty. ROLLUP FILTERS: Require a nested aggregation type wrapper. Do NOT use flat filters like {"rollup": {"contains": "value"}}. Instead use one of: (1) {"rollup": {"any": {<condition>}}} - matches if ANY related item satisfies condition; (2) {"rollup": {"every": {<condition>}}} - matches if ALL related items satisfy condition; (3) {"rollup": {"none": {<condition>}}} - matches if NO related items satisfy condition; (4) {"rollup": {"number": {<number_condition>}}} - for number rollup aggregations (count, sum, avg, etc.); (5) {"rollup": {"date": {<date_condition>}}} - for date rollup aggregations (earliest, latest). Inside rollup.any/every/none, use the filter type matching the underlying property type. Compound filters use 'and' or 'or' arrays: {"and": [<filter1>, <filter2>]} or {"or": [<filter1>, <filter2>]}.

page_size.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–100). Defaults to 100 if omitted.

database_id.description: The UUID of the Notion database to query (32 character hex string, with hyphens or without). IMPORTANT: This must be a DATABASE ID, not a page ID. Page IDs and database IDs are different things. If you have a page URL/ID, that is NOT the same as the database ID - inline databases within pages have their own separate database IDs distinct from the parent page ID. Use NOTION_SEARCH_NOTION_PAGE or NOTION_FETCH_DATABASE to discover the correct database ID. The database must be shared with your integration.

start_cursor.description: Cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor` for fetching the next page. Use the exact cursor value returned by Notion.

Supports bulk operations with per-item error handling.

NOTION_UPDATE_ROW_DATABASE.description: Updates a specific row/page within a Notion database by its page UUID (row_id). IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION: This action updates INDIVIDUAL ROWS (pages) in a database, NOT the database structure. - To update a ROW/PAGE: Use THIS action with `row_id` (the page UUID) - To update DATABASE SCHEMA (columns, properties, title): Use NOTION_UPDATE_SCHEMA_DATABASE with `database_id` REQUIRED: `row_id` is MANDATORY. This is the UUID of the specific page/row to update. Do NOT pass `database_id` to this action - that parameter does not exist here. Common issues: (1) Use UUID from page URL, not the full URL (2) Ensure page is shared with integration (3) Match property names exactly as in database (4) Use 'status' type for Status properties, not 'select' (5) Retry on 409 Conflict errors (concurrent updates) Supports updating properties, icon, cover, or archiving the row.

icon.description: The emoji to be used as the icon for the page. Must be a single emoji character (e.g., '😻', '🤔'). Empty strings or whitespace-only values are ignored.

cover.description: URL of an external image to be used as the cover for the page (e.g., 'https://google.com/image.png'). Empty strings or whitespace-only values are ignored.

row_id.description: REQUIRED: The page UUID of the database row to update. This is a PAGE ID (not a database ID). A database row in Notion is actually a page - use the page's UUID here. Format: 32-character UUID with hyphens (e.g., '59833787-2cf9-4fdf-8782-e53db20768a5'). NOT a URL or page title. Find this ID in the page URL or via 'Copy link' in Notion. NOTE: To update DATABASE structure/schema, use NOTION_UPDATE_SCHEMA_DATABASE instead. This action only updates individual rows/pages within a database.

delete_row.description: If true, the row (page) will be archived, effectively deleting it from the active view. If the page is already archived, the action will return success with the current page state. If false, the row will be updated with other provided data.

type.description: Type of the property. Common types: title (ONE per database), rich_text, number, select (for dropdowns), multi_select, date, people, files, checkbox, url, email, phone_number, relation. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use 'select' for dropdown properties - NOT 'status'. The 'status' type is a SPECIAL Notion property type (with 'To-do', 'In progress', 'Complete' groups) that most databases do NOT have. If your property shows a simple dropdown list, use 'select' even if the property is NAMED 'Status'. Read-only/unsupported types (auto-skipped): created_time, created_by, last_edited_time, last_edited_by, formula, rollup, unique_id, place. Title and rich_text values are written as literal plain text and split into Notion rich-text objects when needed.

value.description:
Value formatted according to the property type:
- title, rich_text - literal text string. Values longer than 2,000 UTF-16 units are split across Notion rich-text objects; oversized values fail before writing instead of being truncated.
- number - numeric string ex. "23.4"
- select - single option name (no commas). For multiple values, use multi_select.
- multi_select - comma separated values ex. "India,USA"
- date - ISO 8601. Single: "2021-05-11". Range: "2021-05-11/2021-05-15" (slash-separated).
- people - comma separated USER UUIDs (not names). Use NOTION_LIST_USERS to find UUIDs.
- relation - comma separated PAGE UUIDs (not titles). Use NOTION_QUERY_DATABASE to find UUIDs.
- url - a URL string.
- files - comma separated HTTPS URLs only (no file:// or http://).
- checkbox - "True" or "False"

properties.description: List of properties to update. Each property requires: (1) 'name' - exact property name as shown in Notion, (2) 'type' - the property type (title, rich_text, number, select, status, multi_select, date, people, relation, checkbox, url, email, phone_number, files), (3) 'value' - formatted according to type. IMPORTANT: Verify property names exist in the database and match the exact case. Use 'status' type for Status properties, NOT 'select'. Properties not listed will remain unchanged.
